result.topic_en: Gauss expresses the theta-type functions P, Q, R (two-variable and one-variable) as infinite products in terms of the function Fx = (1-x)(1-xx)(1-x^3)..., and derives relations among them, ending with a formula for Fx in terms of P, Q, R.
result.transcription:
Endlich wollen wir durch das Functionalzeichen $F$ in dieser Abh. das
unendliche Product ausdrücken
$Fx = (1-x)(1-xx)(1-x^3)(1-x^4)\cdots$
In diesen Zeichen erscheinen die beiden letzten Theoreme so
[4] $P(x,y) = (1+xy)(1+\frac{x}{y})(1+x^3y)(1+\frac{x^3}{y})(1+x^5y)(1+\frac{x^5}{y})\cdots Fxx$
[5] $R(x,y) = x^{\frac14}(y^{\frac12}+y^{-\frac12})(1+xxy)(1+\frac{xx}{y})(1+x^4y)(1+\frac{x^4}{y})(1+x^6y)(1+\frac{x^6}{y})\cdots Fxx$
Und so ist offenbar
[6] $Q(x,y) = (1-xy)(1-\frac{x}{y})(1-x^3y)(1-\frac{x^3}{y})(1-x^5y)(1-\frac{x^5}{y})\cdots Fxx$
ferner indem man $y=1$ setzt
[7] $Px = (1+x)^2(1-xx)(1+x^3)^2(1-x^4)(1+x^5)^2(1-x^6)\cdots$
[8] $Qx = (1-x)^2(1-xx)(1-x^3)^2(1-x^4)(1-x^5)^2(1-x^6)\cdots$
[9] $Rx = 2x^{\frac14}(1+xx)^2(1-xx)(1+x^4)^2(1-x^4)(1+x^6)^2(1-x^6)\cdots$
Substituirt man hier für $1+x = \frac{1-xx}{1-x}$, $1+x^3 = \frac{1-x^6}{1-x^3}$ u.s.w.
so verwandeln sich diese Ausdrücke in folgende
[10] $Px = \frac{(Fxx)^5}{(Fx)^2(Fx^4)^2}$
[11] $Qx = \frac{(Fx)^2}{Fxx}$
[12] $Rx = 2x^{\frac14}\frac{(Fx^4)^2}{Fxx}$
Hieraus ergibt sich ferner
[13] $Px.Qx = (Qxx)^2$
[14] $Px.Rx = \frac12(R\sqrt{x})^2$ oder was dasselbe ist
$Pxx.Rxx = \frac12(Rx)^2$, $Rxx = \frac{(Rx)^2}{2Pxx}$
$Qxx(Rx)^2 = 4x^{\frac12}.(Fx^4)^3$ also
[15] $Fx = \sqrt[3]{\frac{Q(x^{\frac14}).(Rx^{\frac14})^2}{4x^{\frac18}}} = [-\sqrt[3]{\frac{Px.Qx.Rx}{2x^{\frac18}}}-] \sqrt[3]{\frac{P(x^{\frac14})Qx^{\frac14}Rx^{\frac14}}{2x^{\frac18}}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{(Qx)^2R(x^{\frac14})}{2x^{\frac18}}}$

methods.what: Definition of the Euler product function F
Specialization y=1 giving products for Px, Qx, Rx
Eta-quotient expressions for P, Q, R
Identity P·R = ½ R(√x)^2 and duplication for R
Expression of F as cube root of product of theta functions (Jacobi-type)
